q1_where_the_one_vector_traversal_enters.the_residual_add_is_the_seam: Both paths express the residual as `backend.residual_add(row, &delta)` = `h += delta`. In the hyper-connection topology there is no add: stage 5 `expand_streams` computes `out[k] = post[k]*b + sum_j comb[j,k]*x[j]` — the carry (comb term) and the add (post term) are ONE operation. So the two residual_add call sites (batch 774, 811; decode 464, 497) are exactly what the traversal replaces; nothing upstream of the operator dispatch and nothing inside it changes.

Under a bundle the `residual` argument must be the REDUCED vector (stage 3 output), never the bundle.

q3_where_expansion_the_two_mixes_and_hea.why_sublayer_forward_does_not_drop_in_on: sublayer_forward (hyper_connection.rs:377-399) composes stages 1-5 around `branch: FnOnce(&[f32]) -> Vec<f32>` — ONE position, ONE vector. The batch traversal runs the operator over ALL positions in one call (softmax 729, ConvQkv 707, FFN-many 833) or as one sequential flat call (KDA 640). So the batch path must run stages 1-3 per position, the operator over the batch, then stage 5 per position; every stage is `pub` on its own, so this costs no new arithmetic, and `sublayer_forward` stays the single-position reference the decode path can call directly. This is the concrete way wave 17's reference does NOT map 1:1 onto traversal structure.
q3_where_expansion_the_two_mixes_and_hea.exit_reduction: After the last layer the state is a bundle. When ComponentOpPlan.hyper_connection_head is Some: `head_reduce(x, streams, hidden, HeadWeights{reduce_fn, base, scale}, norm_eps, hc.sinkhorn_eps)` -> `[hidden]` -> final_norm -> output_head, unchanged from there. head_reduce takes a `norm_eps`; the plan carries it per LAYER (declared_norm_eps), not per component — the executor must name its source (a freeze decision; equal on both real checkpoints). Only on a whole-stack slice.
q3_where_expansion_the_two_mixes_and_hea.when_no_head_is_declared_glm: The layers ran and the bundle exists; there is no declared reduction and this build must not invent one. Two honest shapes exist today: (a) ExecutionSlice::LayerRange (prepared.rs:70-73) — bundle in, bundle out, no entry expansion, no exit reduction, no head needed — which is the per-layer contract the GLM constraint asks for and already exists as a seam; (b) a whole-stack run that emits every layer plane and then refuses at the exit with a named reason. (b) conflicts with the refuse-before-any-output doctrine at traverse:358-364 unless the refusal is decided up front and the caller asked for planes only. Which shape the witness uses is a freeze decision; the recon records that (a) needs no new contract.

q4_which_intermediate_state_can_be_tappe.why_none_of_them_is_a_witness: Every existing tap is a `[hidden]`-wide residual or sublayer input. A single-stream traversal of the same plan produces all of them. Width `streams·hidden` would prove a bundle EXISTS, not that the split ran: a traversal that replicated the residual and averaged it back would carry a bundle and produce these taps too.
